purpose: Number-theory SFT on Lean-checked competition proofs, about half with informal reasoning between tactics; before the GPU pass-rate map and GRPO
initial_policy: SFT v2 final checkpoint (lean_sft_20261009_v2, cpu-angad formal_rl/sft_checkpoints/v2_final)
data: formal_rl/nt_sft_v5 from scripts/data/build_nt_sft_data.py --problems nt_splits_v3/sft_problems.txt on nt_pool_v2: 1,088 train + 65 eval-loss examples from 553 train-split problems (550 Goedel proofs with comments, 603 Lean Workbook proofs without). nt_splits_v3 keeps out of SFT the 25% held-out proof problems (the RL hole tasks come only from them), train statements with token Jaccard >= 0.85 to a validation or test statement or >= 0.7 to any miniF2F statement, and the 17 vacuous train statements; validation and test statements not read. Replaces nt_sft_v2 (1,593 + 96 rows, 813 problems) and nt_sft_v4. run_sft.py reads sft_train.jsonl and sft_val.jsonl, so stage train.jsonl and val.jsonl under those names
ablation_arm: Interleaving ablation: the same config with data formal_rl/nt_sft_v5_nocomments (build_nt_sft_data.py --strip-comments, same problems file): the same 1,088 + 65 examples in the same order, with block and line comments removed from every proof
precision: FP32 master weights and AdamW moments, BF16 autocast
instance: one NVIDIA L40S (AWS g6e.2xlarge), on demand
notes: Token lengths measured on nt_sft_v1 (Qwen tokenizer, chat template): train median 300, p90 727, max 1,809; 44 of 1,611 exceed 1,024, none exceed 2,048. Batch 2 x 2,048 keeps at most 4,096 tokens per micro-batch, the size SFT v2 ran without OOM. Evaluation of this model needs max_new_tokens of at least 1,024, because commented proofs are longer than the 256-token cap used so far.
